quickfire.question: In a circular array queue, after inserting at rear, the new rear index is: (q->rear + 1) _____ MAX

routineWriter.questionText: Write the enqueue routine for a circular array-based queue.

commonMistakes.description: Overflow check must use size, not rear — a circular queue's rear can wrap to 0 even when full
Modulo wraps rear around — omitting % MAX causes rear to go out of bounds
Size must be tracked separately — front/rear positions alone cannot distinguish empty from full in circular queues

quickfire.question: In a circular queue dequeue, after removing from front, the new front index is: (q->front + 1) _____ MAX

routineWriter.questionText: Write the dequeue routine for a circular array-based queue.

commonMistakes.description: Underflow guard uses size — front == rear is ambiguous (could be empty or full)
Read from front BEFORE advancing it — advancing first reads the wrong element
Circular advance — same modulo pattern as enqueue's rear advance

quickfire.question: A deque (double-ended queue) differs from a regular queue because:
options: It stores values in sorted order
Insertion and deletion can happen at both ends
quickfire.answer: Insertion and deletion can happen at both ends
